headline: Taiwan to pay $314 cash to every resident in 2027, funded by AI server boom
summary: Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te announced a NT$10,000 (approx. $314 USD) payout for every resident in 2027, financed by a $7.4 billion dividend from surging AI-driven export revenues.
details: Taiwan plans to distribute NT$10,000 (approx. $314 USD) to every resident in 2027, as announced by President Lai Ching-te. This initiative is funded by a NT$235.7 billion ($7.4 billion USD) allocation from the central government budget. The President stated this ensures the "AI dividend can be shared by all."

The significant payout is attributed to a global surge in demand for AI, high-performance computing, and cloud services. This demand has boosted Taiwan's projected 2027 general revenue to NT$3.93 trillion, allowing the payment without new borrowing.

Taiwan's economy is experiencing rapid growth, with the DGBAS raising its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 11.05%, the fastest pace since 1987. Merchandise exports are expected to reach $903.6 billion this year, a 41.19% jump and the sharpest increase in five decades.

AI servers and related goods are projected to account for almost 40% of these exports, up from 30% in 2025. Taiwanese manufacturers like Foxconn, Quanta, and Wistron produce most of the world's AI servers, driving this export boom.

While the tech sector thrives, President Lai acknowledged that the boom has not equally benefited everyone, particularly workers in services, traditional industries, and small businesses. Non-tech exports saw only an 8.6% rise in the first seven months, significantly lower than the overall rate.

This isn't the first such payout; Taiwan issued an identical NT$10,000 per person starting in November 2025, but that was for tariff and inflation relief. The Presidential Office has yet to confirm eligibility, timing, or distribution methods for the upcoming 2027 payment.

The opposition Kuomintang and Taiwan People's Party, who control the legislature, have already demanded the payment be doubled to NT$20,000. Given a recent record delay in passing the 2026 budget, a smooth review for the 2027 budget is not guaranteed.

headline_marked: Darwin Family: [[VIDRAFT's training-free model merging framework hits 86.9% on GPQA Diamond]]
headline: Darwin Family: VIDRAFT's training-free model merging framework hits 86.9% on GPQA Diamond
summary: VIDRAFT's Darwin Family framework improves LLM reasoning through evolutionary parameter recombination, achieving 86.9% on GPQA Diamond without any gradient training. Its flagship Darwin-27B-Opus model even outperforms its fully-trained parent models.
details: VIDRAFT, a Korean AI startup, has published the Darwin Family framework, which significantly improves LLM reasoning. Their flagship model, Darwin-27B-Opus, scored 86.9% on GPQA Diamond, ranking 6th globally among 1,252 evaluated models.

The core innovation is a training-free model merging process. Instead of costly retraining, it combines the weight parameters of two existing models—a strong generalist and a reasoning specialist—to create an 'offspring' that inherits the best of both.

Named after Charles Darwin, the framework uses an evolutionary algorithm. It treats candidate merge configurations as individuals, applies selection pressure, and evolves towards better-performing combinations over generations.

Darwin Family's technical approach includes MRI Diagnostic Importance Scoring. This 'scans' parent models to estimate each layer's contribution to reasoning, informing an initial mixing ratio for parameter merging.

Beyond initial scoring, an evolutionary search refines the merge configuration. Each recipe is encoded as a 14-dimensional 'genome vector,' which is then optimized through population generation, evaluation, crossover, and mutation.

A scalar parameter, τ (tau), called MRI-Trust Fusion, balances diagnostic guidance with exploratory flexibility. Crucially, τ is not hand-tuned but learned by the evolutionary process itself, consistently converging to an optimal range.

The entire process operates on fixed, pre-existing model weights, requiring no gradient-based training or weight updates. Candidate merge configurations are evaluated using inference-time benchmark scores, making it highly efficient.

Model merging works because reasoning capabilities are largely encoded during pre-training and remain stable. By selectively and importance-weightedly combining parameters from compatible parent models, the framework recombines complementary capability 'regions' effectively.
